method: Only child processes launched for this diagnosis; read-only Toolhelp/CPU counters every50ms. The two stack cases additionally briefly pause the child AMD worker after1.2s; no symbols downloaded and no external process, driver, registry, priority or application altered.
limitations: Thread times are lifetime counters, not exact frame-window intervals. Entry-module labels are not CPU stack samples. AMD symbols are private: large-offset nearest exports printed by DbgHelp must not be interpreted as function names. Raw/backend initial quiet controls sleep3s without SDL event pumping; pumped cases have explicit SDL event pumping. Visible cases had cached focus0; they do not establish foreground behavior or the cause of the first user trace.
observation: All26 before/after worker stack samples include NtWaitForSingleObject -> WaitForSingleObjectEx -> amdvlk64.dll+0x385165 -> +0x24da25. Local disassembly sets the wait timeout to0 and the caller retry branch calls Sleep(0). This identifies polling in the observed driver thread, not the exact Vulkan API cause.
controls: Raw device/timeline creation and fence/timeline signaling, offscreen rendering, and WSI surface creation without presentation do not show this high-CPU worker. Four actual WSI presents then3s quiet do, for Reference/SDF/compute and FIFO. Visible-but-unfocused quiet controls also do. Pumping during the quiet interval, destroying the surface, three extra created/destroyed overlay surfaces, disabling implicit layers or only OBS in this child and a host-released pending timeline wait do not stop the one busy worker. This does not measure active capture cost on the real user workload. True-foreground control remains open.
